summary.one_liner: MacDown is an open source Markdown editor for macOS (OS X), released under the MIT License.
summary.what_it_does: MacDown is a Markdown editor for OS X, described as inspired by Chen Luo's Mou. The README says it renders Markdown to HTML using Hoedown and provides syntax highlighting in the editor via PEG Markdown Highlight, with Prism used for code block highlighting. It ships several editor themes and CSS files extracted from Mou, including Mou Night, Tomorrow, Writer, Clearness and GitHub variants. Installation is by downloading the MacDown.app.zip from the releases page or via Homebrew Cask. Developers can build it from source in Xcode using a workspace, CocoaPods and Bundler. Translations are handled through Transifex.
use_cases: Writing and previewing Markdown documents on a Mac
Editing README or documentation files with live rendering
Trying Mou-style Markdown editing with bundled themes
Building MacDown from source for local development
Editing Markdown with syntax-highlighted code blocks
how_to_run: Download MacDown.app.zip from the latest releases page, unzip, and drag the app to Applications
notable: Derived from the idea of Chen Luo's Mou editor, with several Mou themes included
Uses Hoedown for Markdown-to-HTML rendering and Prism for code block highlighting
caveats: Building from source requires the OS X SDK 10.14 or later, Git and Bundler
Old CocoaPods versions are not supported
The README notes the app does not update immediately when changes are made, so the development version may differ from releases
